subject: [PATCH v3 2/7] selftests/mm: check MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT range handling

2026-10-19.patch_summary: This patch adds four new test cases to the selftests/mm/madv_cold_pageout.c file to verify the behavior of the madvise(2) system call when dealing with zero-length ranges, unaligned start addresses, and unmapped gaps in the range. The tests check that a zero-length range is accepted, an unaligned start address is rejected, and an unmapped gap in the range results in ENOMEM errors for both MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT hints. Only MADV_PAGEOUT has an observable effect on pages around the gap, so only its behavior is checked in this case.

reviews.author: Sarthak Sharma
reviews.summary: Identified the patch as good to go, with no major issues or concerns.
reviews.raw_body:
On 10/19/26 10:42 PM, Gregory Price (Meta) wrote:
> madvise(2) accepts a zero-length range, rejects an unaligned start, and
> reports an unmapped gap in the range with ENOMEM while still applying the
> advice to the mapped pages on either side.
> 
> Check each of these for both hints. Around the gap, only MADV_PAGEOUT has
> an effect the test can observe, so only MADV_PAGEOUT is checked for
> paging out both neighbors, and only if MADV_PAGEOUT can swap at all.
> Both hints' ENOMEM is checked first, so it is covered without swap.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
Looks good to me.

Reviewed-by: Sarthak Sharma <sarthak.sharma@arm.com>

2026-10-28.patch_summary: This patch series introduces selftests to verify the handling of MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT range boundaries, including zero-length ranges, unaligned starts, and unmapped gaps.
